snippets.output: Antituberculosis drugs are known to cause hepatotoxicity.
Isoniazid is known to cause hepatotoxicity.
Rifampin is known to cause hepatotoxicity.
Pyrazinamide is known to cause hepatotoxicity.
Antituberculosis drugs are known to cause hepatotoxicity, including isoniazid, rifampin, and pyrazinamide.

Elevated liver enzymes may indicate hepatotoxicity, a significant adverse effect of antituberculosis drugs in a 27-year-old man with positive QuantiFERON gold testing who was started on tuberculosis treatment; hepatotoxicity could warrant discontinuation of the medications until liver function normalizes.
Pyrazinamide is associated with causing hyperuricemia, which can be uncomfortable.

Hyperuricemia typically does not necessitate discontinuation of treatment in a 27-year-old man with tuberculosis treatment initiation after positive QuantiFERON gold testing, but treatment may be discontinued if hyperuricemia leads to symptomatic gout.

Hyperuricemia typically does not necessitate discontinuation of tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man with positive QuantiFERON gold testing, but tuberculosis treatment may be discontinued if hyperuricemia leads to severe uric acid nephropathy.
Ethambutol can cause optic neuritis, a serious adverse effect that manifests as visual disturbances and can lead to permanent vision loss if not addressed promptly.
Optic neuritis is an indication for discontinuation of ethambutol.
Discontinuation of ethambutol in a 27-year-old man with positive QuantiFERON gold testing who was started on tuberculosis treatment prevents permanent damage from optic neuritis.
Isoniazid can cause peripheral neuropathy, and isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy is caused by pyridoxine (vitamin B6) deficiency.
Peripheral neuropathy can often be prevented and managed by supplementing pyridoxine.
Peripheral neuropathy typically does not require discontinuation of isoniazid.
Discontinuation of isoniazid may be necessary in a 27-year-old man with tuberculosis treatment initiation if symptoms of peripheral neuropathy are severe.
Rifampin can cause red-orange discoloration of body fluids.
Red-orange discoloration of body fluids is a benign side effect of rifampin.
Red-orange discoloration of body fluids does not necessitate discontinuation of tuberculosis treatment in a 27-year-old man with positive QuantiFERON gold testing.

For the 27-year-old man with fatigue, cough, 15-pound weight loss over 3 weeks, recent release from prison, intravenous drug use in prison, and positive QuantiFERON gold testing who was started on tuberculosis treatment, the most likely indication to discontinue treatment would be optic neuritis.
